'''Sylvia Chin-Pi Lu''' (1928–2014) was a Taiwanese-American mathematician specializing in [[commutative algebra]] who was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the 1990 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Kyoto]].<ref name="ams-obit">{{cite web |title=Sylvia Chin-Pi Lu (1928-2014) |url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=2311 |website=American Mathematical Society |accessdate=28 June 2019}}</ref> Less than 5% of ICM speakers in algebra and number theory have been women, placing Lu in a rarefied group in this "hall of fame for mathematics".<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Mihaljević |first1=Helena |last2=Roy |first2=Marie-Françoise |title=A data analysis of women's trails among ICM speakers |eprint=1903.02543 |class=math.HO |year=2019 }}</ref> Lu's most highly cited papers are on the properties of prime submodules.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lu, Chin-Pi |url=https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/search/author.html?mrauthid=116400 |website=MathSciNet: Mathematical Reviews |publisher=American Mathematical Society |accessdate=28 June 2019}}</ref>

==Education==

Lu received her dissertation from [[The Pennsylvania State University]] in 1963, under the direction of Raymond Ayoub.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Lu |first1=Chin-Pi |title=The Ring of Formal Power Series in a Countably Infinite Number of Indeterminates (dissertation) |date=1963 |publisher=The Pennsylvania State University}}</ref>
